cells.tense: You are narrowing what matters here, one honest cut at a time.
cells.ask: Each day this week, write down one thing you decided and the single reason that settled it. No audience. On the last day, read the week back and let the pattern show you.
cells.core:
You're at the work with your own hands on it, and the thinking behind it is private and exact. You keep testing the distinctions until they hold, and you keep holding when the results come slowly. That combination is rarer than it sounds: attention sharp enough to sort, steadiness deep enough to stay.

The thing that usually bends this is the push to arrive. You don't have to force the pace. What needs to come down will come down on its own, and the practice goes cleaner when you let it. Make one good call a day for a week and let the record show you what you actually chose.
cells.sheetLine: You decide what's true here, slowly and on purpose.

cells.tense: You will have it sorted before anyone sees it, or it will not be worth showing.
cells.ask: Pick one unfinished thing today and call it done at the level it stands. Tell one person what getting it this far cost you, then stop for the day.
cells.core:
The refining has gone past where it helps. You're holding a finished version of the thing in your head, testing each angle against a future where someone is finally satisfied. The scrutiny has become the work, and it keeps you where no one else can reach you — private turned into sealed.

The cost is plain: the care that was meant to serve the thing is now what's holding it back. You don't have to finish it in there. Hand over what exists at the size it is, let one person hear what the effort took, and let the day close on it.

cells.tense: You used to sit with a problem and cut it clean, and the sitting stopped.
cells.ask: Trade one small thing this week: give someone what they asked for, and ask them for one thing you need back. Keep both halves even and spoken.
cells.core:
A tangled problem used to get a quiet hour and come out sorted — a few hard calls made, the rest set down, and you walked away steadier than you started. That steadiness carried the long stretches, and it kept you in the room while other people were still arguing about where to stand.

Lately it isn't carrying much. The figuring gets done in fragments with nowhere to land, or it doesn't get done at all, and the weight sits on you without being picked up. One fair trade, seen through both sides, puts some weight back on the muscle and makes the next clear call easier to reach.
cells.sheetLine: The sitting stopped, and the weight just stays on you.

cells.tense: You are already sorting what counts from what doesn't, and calling it the way things went.
cells.ask: Name one hour this week where you sat with a real problem and shaped it. Tell one person it was your hour and what it made, then let it be counted.
cells.core:
The careful thinking is happening, and it looks like this when it's going well: you take a mess, sit with it, and come out holding the one distinction that was carrying the weight. People feel the difference and act on it. That part is already running.

What's missing is the saying-so. You cut the distinction that no one else made — in a conversation, a plan, a thing that needed fixing — and then describe it as the situation sorting itself out. The hour was yours. Name it once, out loud, and let one other person hear it before it goes back to being nobody's.
cells.sheetLine: The careful thinking is happening. You just haven't claimed it as yours.

attempts.check: The record supports a private, careful, distinguished form of thinking seated in the body's endurance; it does not say the person actually does this practice daily, or that any particular structure in their life has already fallen. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't get to a desk at all, my body is the thing that's failing me, not my attention.' The ask survives that: writing down the single call and the reason each day is a discipline anyone can enter without money, energy, safety or time, and it doesn't depend on my read being right. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one about the body being where the honest thinking sits — the record says the mental work is private and personal in the Body house, not that the body is a reliable instrument; I keep it out. The instrument in the fourth cell — the accumulated notes, drafts, small daily records — is the founder's picture, not the person's; I narrow it to 'what you already kept and never counted' and let them fill it.
